dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Before writing any compiler code, systematically read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py, and filter.json (computed per-suite test counts 146/221/413=780), sampled all three suites, mapped the wacc chapter structure (chapters 1-18), counted chapter distribution in the filter, and sampled gcc-torture's hardest cases (bitfields, struct passing). Also verified rustc/gcc toolchain availability. This is thorough corpus characterization matching the level-8 anchor.

After first full run, immediately got per-suite breakdown (c_testsuite 131/146, wacc 195/221, gcc 157/413), grouped failures by suite, and derived feature priorities from evidence (identified param-name loss as the cause of chapter-9 failures) rather than assumption.

Drilled into the exact C corner when a class failed: built a precise mental model of C integer promotion / common_type, then long-negation sign-extension (traced 'movq $1;negl %eax' producing 0xffffffff), reasoning from emitted assembly back into codegen design — level-10 'suites as evolving spec' behavior.

Reasoned explicitly about the SysV ABI for struct-by-value: structs <=16 bytes in registers, hidden pointer for large returns, computed struct sizes/alignment (short+long+short=12 bytes), and scoped the feature accordingly — ABI details worked out against real test cases though partly from recall.
Final ~40 steps are entirely a hung-terminal recovery loop with no orientation content; investigation had effectively concluded earlier at ~96.7%. Does not add or detract from the dimension.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's orientation clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it systematically characterized the whole corpus (suite sizes, wacc chapter distribution, hard-case sampling) and derived a feature-priority ordering from evidence before building (level 8), and it sustained failure-driven investigation throughout — drilling into integer promotion, sign-extension, and the SysV struct-passing ABI, feeding each finding back into codegen (level 10). It falls just short of a perfect 10 because several ABI details were asserted from recall and reasoning over emitted assembly rather than verified against an independent reference, placing it at a strong 9.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Agent explicitly chose to build a 'comprehensive single-file compiler initially', writing the entire pipeline (ast/lex/preproc/parse/sema/codegen) in one push before any build — the whole-language-at-once pattern, not an ordered feature progression.
First build then full-suite run establishes a baseline pass % (61.9%→88.3%). Progress is measured by full-suite percentage rather than a planned per-feature milestone sequence.

Iteration is reactive: dump failures, group by pattern/suite, fix, re-run, note new cumulative % (89.5%→92.1%). Feature order determined by what tests flag, not by dependency ordering planned in advance.

Later stages group remaining failures by feature (struct passing, bitfields, complex/vector types) and make tractability judgments to tackle or skip — a form of milestone selection with test done-signals, but still no explicit dependency-ordered plan; no TodoWrite used across the whole run.
Trajectory ends with the terminal stuck; agent declares done at 96.7%, confirming the process was continuous test-driven bug-fixing rather than a closing sequence of certified milestones.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent attempted the whole language at once (anchor 0's core clause) rather than an ordered, dependency-sequenced milestone progression, and never maintained an explicit per-feature milestone plan (falling well short of anchors 5/8). However, it consistently used full-suite pass percentages and grouped test-failure subsets as concrete done-signals, and prioritized remaining features by impact/tractability — behavior that exceeds anchor 3's 'no per-milestone success check.' This places it at a 4: monolithic build with reactive, test-checked feature triage rather than a designed staged progression.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: After the full-suite baseline, the agent isolates individual failing tests (00044, 00053, 00117, 00162, 00199), runs each binary alone checking exit codes, and at step 52 emits assembly with -S to diagnose why 00117 returns 160 instead of 0 — per-construct isolation plus asm inspection.

Explicitly bisects a failing gcc-torture test by writing successive minimal /tmp/test.c repros ('Let me bisect'), running each with exit-code check, then dumping and reading emitted assembly to spot spurious push/pop and double-evaluation of args.

Writes minimal repros (/tmp/test.c, /tmp/test2.c) and reads generated asm instruction-by-instruction ('FOUND IT! leaq a(%rip)... movzbq %al'), reasoning about cast_value byte-size logic against specific emitted instructions — verification at single-instruction granularity.

Saves full-suite output to /tmp/r2..r6.txt and compares against prior runs to detect regressions ('Net: fixed sign_extend but added 3 new failures'), then reverts a net-negative change; confirms promotion/sign-extension edge semantics (movslq) with targeted cast tests.

Late in the run still constructs minimal repros for bitfield compound-assignment, traces the exact push/pop register ordering in emitted asm, and confirms expected runtime values — sustained tight loop to the end.

dimensions.reasoning: Throughout the trajectory the agent runs a deliberate, fine-grained verification loop: minimal C reproductions, per-test isolation, repeated -S assembly inspection read against expected instructions, checking both compile success and runtime exit values, plus saving and diffing suite outputs to catch regressions and confirm promotion/sign-extension edge cases. This matches anchor 8 squarely. It stops short of 10 because the asm 'diffing' and failure categorization are done manually by reading rather than via reusable bisection harnesses/tooling.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: Established per-suite baseline counts (c_testsuite 131/146, wacc 195/221, gcc_torture 157/413) then re-ran to confirm the jump to 689/780 (88.3%), showing an aggregate + per-suite picture from early on.

Systematic regression watch: after each change re-ran suite, saved FAIL snapshots to /tmp/rN.txt and diffed to name newly-broken tests (sign_extend, bswap-2, pr53465); reverted the call-site casting change once confirmed net-negative — explicit thrash detection and correction.
Repeatedly reasoned in net terms ('Net change: lost some, gained some. Net is -3', 'Slight regression... revert') — using regression deltas rather than raw totals to accept/reject changes.
Continued the snapshot-diff discipline (r12–r16), tracked climbing totals (94.9% → 95.6% → 96.7%) and used remaining-failure lists to pick next targets (bitfields, structs, designated init).
At the end, when the terminal hung, correctly reported last confirmed state (754/780, 96.7%) from its tracked ledger rather than guessing, showing the pass-count picture was maintained to the end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept a structured, current pass/fail picture by suite and by named failing test, and — crucially — instituted an explicit newly-broken vs newly-fixed regression check (numbered FAIL-list diffs) after essentially every significant change, reverting net-negative edits and using the failure trend to choose where to work next; this squarely matches the level-8 anchor and touches level-10 behaviors (thrash detection, effort allocation to highest-yield failures). It falls short of a full 10 because tracking was per-suite plus individual tests rather than a continuously maintained per-feature-category ledger, so I place it at 8.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Diagnosed root cause of a cluster of argument-passing failures — parser's Type::Func discarded param names — and refactored parse_postfix_decl to carry names through, rather than patching codegen. Structural fix that jumped pass rate 61%->88%.

Recognized a systemic limitation ('my codegen doesn't apply integer promotions before binary ops'), and redesigned gen_binary to cast operands to a common type — a codegen-strategy change addressing a whole class of int/long failures, not one test.

Tried call-site argument casting, observed a net regression across runs, and decisively reverted rather than stubbornly patching around it — reasoning explicitly about net trade-off. Shows avoiding needless churn.

When ad-hoc statement-expression handling was falsified, changed the AST representation itself by adding an Expr::Block/StmtExpr variant and wiring codegen — representation-level redesign when the approach couldn't fit.

Distinguished local bugs from structural limits: identified struct-by-value passing as a major missing feature and implemented the <=16-byte SysV path, while explicitly scoping out floats/vectors/complex/large-struct-return as too costly for the remaining gain.

Recurring weakness: the same root cause (values held in 64-bit regs not sign-extended) was patched locally in ~6 separate places (cast_value, return, pointer arith, switch, negation, args) without ever unifying a canonical-width invariant — symptom-level fixes for one underlying class.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures and undertakes genuine targeted redesign — carrying param names through the parser, adding common-type promotion in gen_binary, introducing an AST variant for statement-expressions, and adding struct-by-value ABI — while reasoning about trade-offs (reverting the net-negative call-casting change), matching much of the level-8 description. It falls short of 8+ because a recurring sign-extension/width class of bugs was patched piecemeal in many locations rather than unified into a single structural invariant, showing the local-fix tendency of the level-3 anchor. This blend of strong root-cause redesign with some persistent symptom-patching places it at 7.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Up-front deliberate staged pipeline: separate ast.rs, lex.rs, preproc.rs, parse.rs, sema.rs, codegen.rs modules created with explicit roles — sema computes struct/union sizes/offsets/alignments, resolves typedefs, annotates expressions with types; codegen uses a stack-machine model. Clear lexer/parser/analysis/codegen separation with reasoned representations for types and scopes.

The chosen representation supported a large feature set immediately — first working build passed 61.9%, then jumped to 88.3% after a small param-name plumbing fix, indicating AST/type/scope structures were general enough to absorb many features without redesign.

Type-aware sized codegen (32-bit vs 64-bit ops, sign-extension), struct/union member offsets, and bitfield layout were expressible in the representation — the hard 'type-aware codegen' anchor items were designed in, not merely patched.

Struct tag scoping was recognized as needed but deliberately special-cased ('I don't scope them, just...' — replace only if incomplete) rather than designing proper scoped tag tables — a gap short of the level-8/10 clean-design ideal.

SysV struct-by-value passing added late as a bolt-on for specific torture tests; statement-expressions returning structs couldn't be absorbed and were skipped — some breadth handled by special-casing rather than by the original design.

Module boundaries (parse/sema/codegen/lex) persisted and were edited in place throughout the whole horizon — no monolithic collapse or wholesale representation rewrite; the staged pipeline held as scope grew.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent established a coherent, distinctly-staged pipeline up front (exceeding anchor 5) and deliberately designed representations for several hard parts — sized/typed values enabling type-aware codegen, struct/union layout in sema, symbol/param tracking, lvalue handling — which is squarely in anchor-8 territory and is corroborated by the foundation absorbing most features immediately (62%→88%→96%). It falls short of a clean 8-10 because key hard parts (struct tag scoping, struct-by-value/statement-expr returns) were special-cased or bolted on rather than designed to slot in with minimal disruption, so breadth was only partly absorbed by design. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
